I have a marker to share about the rock formation on Lake Michigan at Sheboygan, Wisconsin’s North Point Park, but first must share video of the massive number of pelicans I saw on it. It turns out American white pelicans hang out on this rock about this time every year as they migrate north 1/2
Although the alewives in Lake Michigan are not native to the Great Lakes, American White Pelicans have no complaints about adding them to the menu. #birds 🪶

In fact American White Pelican's which are born and raised in #Canada should really be called Canadian White Pelican's. This one is flying over the waters of Lake Ontario in Canada. #birds #birding #photography
American White Pelicans breed in the summer in Canadian lakes from Lake Superior in Ontario, and west across Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, British Columbia and in southern Northwest Territory.

We’ll see the White Pelicans migrating along the west end of Lake Erie and it’s wild to see these big birds catch thermals and lift so fast into the sky until they’re dots.
Saw the pelicans today on the way to Morris. Glad they continue to stop in the area on the way to Lake Michigan
Our pelicans have returned to over-winter here from the Great Lakes. We should be able to enjoy them thru March
The pelicans are doing their daily shift. They’ll soon be headed back to the Great Lakes for the summer
Did you see the pelicans yet? I ran into a bunch of them last week near Lake Erie. Was well worth the detour.
Our pelicans on their daily shift. They’ll probably should be leaving us soon for the Great Lakes

NW IL. They come for summer but a few linger. White Pelicans are some of the cool variety of birds on Mississippi Fly way migration route. We had those and cormorants in fall. First winter Pelican I have seen at dam. You may get to see them on lake Michigan.😍
Ah, makes sense. Thanks! I didn’t realize pelicans came that far inland. Have only seen them at the oceans. I’m close enough to Lake Michigan to have lots of seabirds but not them.
Pelicans resting on lake Michigan during their migration! #pelicans
Impressed. Here by Lake Erie, the early peonies are mid bud.

Meant to type Lake Erie! Sorry.😂 See how close they get out there. I saw them out West \ South as well. White Pelicans are only type to go far North. Enormous birds and like cartoons swallow fish and they flap down throats as both struggle.😂 We scream \ laugh every time we see that. Some in fall.😍
There have been more pelicans showing up in Lake Michigan and I’m really hoping to see some this summer
Beautiful! FYI, last summer, I took a trip through Michigan and upper Michigan, and was very surprised to see quite a few white pelicans on Lake Michigan and Lake Superior.
White Pelicans go up Mississippi into Great Lakes.

We get a rare occasional lost pelican. They show up on the south side of Lake Erie more regularly. Hamilton gets one or a few blown off course every few years, too. But I’m talking about the bottom of Kipling Ave, on the waterfront.
This summer another photographer captured brilliant shots downtown!
Forgot abt the pelicans. That’s what made me think southeast. We don’t have them in the Great Lakes.
🩵 White pelicans along the shores of Lake Michigan in Sheboygan Brooke ….
On Sunday while playing Whistling Straits, we saw an American White Pelican flock on Lake Michigan. Same flock a few years later? I think I recognize Petey the Pelican.
Pelicans on Lake Michigan. We are indeed on an inland freshwater sea.
Wait, we've got pelicans on Lake Michigan? In all my years I have never seen one.
